claim:
Let \(\psi:[0,1]\to\mathbb R\) be
\[
\psi(t)=
\begin{cases}
1-t,&0\le t\le\frac18,\\
\frac{11-4t}{12},&\frac18\le t\le\frac12,\\
\frac{1+t}{2},&\frac12\le t\le1,
\end{cases}
\]
and let \(X=\ell_\psi-\ell_\infty\) be the real generalized Day--James plane whose norm is the absolute normalized \(\psi\)-norm when the coordinate product is nonnegative and the \(\ell_\infty\)-norm when it is nonpositive. Then
\[
C_{\mathrm{Pt}}(X)=\frac{13}{9}.
\]
The value is attained by
\[
x=\left(-\frac23,-\frac23\right),\qquad
y=\left(\frac32,-\frac32\right),\qquad
z=\left(\frac56,-\frac{13}{6}\right).
\]
integrity: The proof reconstructs the source-defined octagon, computes a global Hilbert comparison by exact rational edge optimization, and supplies an explicit triple attaining the resulting Ptolemy upper bound. The checker uses exact rational arithmetic only.
scientific_limitations: The theorem concerns one canonical piecewise-linear nonabsolute generalized Day--James octagon and does not classify arbitrary generalized Day--James planes. An unindexed equivalent affine-geometric calculation remains a residual bibliographic risk.
title: Exact Ptolemy constant of the canonical nonabsolute Day--James octagon
